hooks.text: Three hundred eighteen retainers were entombed around Pharaoh Djer.
Ancient Egyptian pharaohs took their household servants into the afterlife.
First Dynasty tombs did not hold the pharaoh alone.

title: Why Did Early Pharaohs Take Their Servants? 😳
description: Explore the First Dynasty royal tombs at Umm el-Qa'ab around 2900 BC, where early Egyptian pharaohs were entombed alongside sacrificed household servants.

beats.text: Three hundred eighteen retainers were entombed around Pharaoh Djer.
beats.visual: Tomb stela of King Djer from Abydos, First Dynasty

beats.text: The royal cemetery of Umm el-Qa'ab near Abydos held the earliest rulers.
beats.visual: Landscape and pottery mounds of Umm el-Qa'ab archaeology site, 20th century

beats.text: English archaeologist Flinders Petrie excavated these subsidiary graves.
beats.visual: Portrait photograph of Flinders Petrie, early 20th century

beats.text: The tombs were sealed simultaneously, suggesting these retainers were sacrificed.
beats.visual: Excavated royal tombs at Abydos showing pottery arrangements, 20th century

beats.text: Forensic re-examination of forty-six skulls revealed fatal perimortem fractures.
beats.visual: Ancient Egyptian skull from Duckworth Collection, University of Cambridge

beats.text: This brutal practice disappeared before the Second Dynasty.
beats.visual: Egyptian shabti figurine from the Middle Kingdom

beats.text: Figurines replaced the retainers entombed around Pharaoh Djer.
beats.visual: Shabti of Tutankhamun illustrating servant figurines
